@graph.name: Foreclosure and distressed property purchase
@graph.description: Guidance on bank-owned and distressed property purchases in Texas.

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, but not automatically. A lower purchase price can be offset by repair costs, carrying costs, and a longer closing. The comparison that matters is total cost against a standard resale in the same area, not list price alone.

mainEntity.name: Can I inspect a foreclosure before buying?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a listed bank-owned property, usually yes. At a courthouse auction, generally no. That difference is the main reason we steer most buyers toward listed distressed property rather than auctions.

mainEntity.name: Do I need cash to buy a foreclosure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for most listed bank-owned homes, which can often be financed. Courthouse auction purchases in Texas typically do require immediate certified funds.
